# Seam 1: Recording Convention Implementation Plan

> For executors: tasks use checkbox syntax; execute in dependency order; a task is done when its
> acceptance check passes. No specific tooling, harness, or skills are assumed.

**Goal:** every work session in a conforming repo leaves one durable, hand-editable session card, handoff consumption becomes an append-only per-action transition log that auto-archives, and the three empty board lanes populate from those records.

**Approach:** doctrine plus enforcement, not a daemon.
Three small shell scripts write the judgment facts (`session-card.sh`, `handoff-log.sh`) and derive everything else (`take-stock.sh`); `lifecycle-lint.sh` grows a class h behind an adoption-date gate, and `board-cards.sh` reads the derived rows into the empty lanes.
Rollout is piloted on this repo and `~/create/sys-prompts-cc`, proven against the sys-prompts-cc handoff case, then propagated by the template-version roll.

**Tech stack:** bash, awk, plain markdown; no new dependencies.

**Source brief:** `docs/briefs/2026-09-07.I52.seam1-recording-convention-brief.md`

## Settled decisions (pinned by the brief, not reopened here)

| Decision                      | Settled value                                                            |
| ---                           | ---                                                                      |
| Session terminal statuses     | closed set of 5: `done`, `blocked`, `handed-off`, `parked`, `aborted`    |
| Died-mid-work                 | an open card with no close, by construction; no status for it            |
| Write path                    | `scripts/session-card.sh open \| log \| close` plus conventions doctrine |
| Card home                     | `docs/sessions/`, one card per session, updated in place                 |
| Filename collision            | `-2` suffix on the slug                                                  |
| Lint class f                  | `docs/sessions/` exempt (class f scans four lanes, sessions is not one)  |
| Done-lane closed-issue window | 60 days, a visible constant in `board-cards.sh`                          |
| Handoff dispositions          | closed set `executed \| superseded`, appended to a transition log        |
| Current state                 | always derived from the log, never a mutable status field                |
| Lint class h                  | consumed-unarchived handoffs, exit non-zero                              |
| Class h gate                  | `lifecycle-lint-since:` in `config/repo-state.md`, on-or-after only      |
| Adoption date                 | the date this run ships the lint class, no template placeholder          |
| Legacy backfill               | the 20 pre-adoption handoffs, human-confirmed table, then archived       |
| Died-mid-work threshold       | 24 hours, a hardcoded visible constant                                   |
| take-stock                    | a new script rebuilding recorded state from git, handoffs, the tracker   |
| Template roll                 | `template-version` 6 to 7, carrying the rubix-autorun drift fix          |
| Pilot pair                    | this repo and `~/create/sys-prompts-cc`                                  |

## Plan-owned design calls (decided here, with reversal paths)

**D9, went-stale as card vs flag: flag, carried on a 13th Card TSV field `marker`.**
A went-stale repo has no work item to be a card of, and the shipped renderer has no non-card row concept, so a went-stale card would need a lane it does not have.
The Card TSV grows one field, `marker`, with values empty, `went-stale`, or `died-mid-work`; `went-stale` rides the repo's git card and `died-mid-work` rides the open session card.
A went-stale repo always gets its git card, so the existing clean-conforming suppression rule gains one exception.
Reversal: emit a separate card row with `source=state` and drop field 13, changing `board-cards.sh` and the two board tests only.

**D13, session card key set and `## Log` format.**
Frontmatter, eight keys, each mapping onto a Card TSV field: `session_card`, `session`, `token`, `title`, `status`, `closed`, `why`, `next`.
`## Log` is append-only, one entry per line, `- <ISO-8601 UTC timestamp> <free text>`.
Reversal: add a key to `session-card.sh`'s emitter and to `take-stock.sh`'s reader; existing cards keep parsing because every reader greps line-anchored keys.

**D20, take-stock invocation surface: `scripts/take-stock.sh <repo-root> [--cards]`.**
Single positional argument matching `lifecycle-lint.sh`'s shape; default output is the human recorded-state report, `--cards` emits the 7-field intermediate TSV that `board-cards.sh` consumes.
Reversal: split `--cards` into a second script; the intermediate TSV contract is unchanged either way.

**Went-stale comparison granularity: calendar day, not seconds.**
A commit made seconds after recording is not stale; a repo is went-stale when its newest commit's `YYYY-MM-DD` is strictly later than its recorded-state date.
Reversal: switch to an hour threshold beside `DIED_MID_WORK_HOURS` in `take-stock.sh`.

**Session status to board lane mapping.**
`open` to `in-session`, `blocked` to `blocked-on-fact`, `handed-off` to `handed-off`, `done` to `done`, `aborted` to `done`, `parked` to `backlog`.
`aborted` lands in `done` because it is terminal and not resumable; the card's `why` says it was aborted.
Reversal: one `case` arm in `board-cards.sh`.

## Global constraints

**Session card format** (the single canonical definition; Task 1 emits it, Task 3 reads it):

```
---
session_card: true
session: <ISO-8601 UTC, when the card was opened>
token: <I52 | B7 | empty>
title: <one line, what this session is>
status: <open | done | blocked | handed-off | parked | aborted>
closed: <ISO-8601 UTC, empty while open>
why: <one line, the reason for the terminal status, empty while open>
next: <one line, the next action>
---

# <title>

## Log

- <ISO-8601 UTC> opened
- <ISO-8601 UTC> <free text, one line per meaningful step>
```

Path: `docs/sessions/<YYYY-MM-DD>.<tokens>.<slug>.md`, slug from the title lowercased with every run of non-alphanumerics collapsed to a dash; on collision the slug takes a `-2` suffix, then `-3`, and so on.
`log` and `close` target the newest card whose `status:` is `open`, resolved by the `session:` timestamp; with no open card both exit non-zero (exit 3), and with two open cards tied to the second they exit non-zero (exit 7) naming the tied files, because a silent pick between same-second cards would target one at random (the doctrine is one card per session, so a tie is already an anomaly worth surfacing).

**Handoff transition log** (the single canonical definition; Task 2 writes it, Task 2 and Task 3 read it):

```
## Transitions

- <ISO-8601 UTC> action <n> <executed|superseded> - <one-line note>
```

Appended to the handoff file itself, append-only, never rewritten.
The actions section is any `## ` heading whose text starts with `Next actions` (prefix match, so `## Next actions, in recommended order` counts); enumerable actions are the lines beginning `- ` or `<n>. ` inside it, numbered 1..N by position.
This matches the real corpus: the three sys-prompts-cc handoffs all carry numbered `1.` items under prefix-variant headings.
Derived state: `live` when the section is absent, when it parses to zero actions with no bulk line, or when any parsed action has no disposition line; `consumed` when every parsed action has one (or a bulk `action 0` line stands in for a zero-action file) and the file sits in `docs/archive/`; `consumed-unarchived` in the same condition with the file still in `docs/handoffs/`.
The bulk `action 0` line is the legacy-backfill shape for files whose actions cannot be enumerated; it is written by `handoff-log.sh disposition <handoff> all <d>` on a zero-action file, and on a file with parsed actions the same verb appends one line per action 1..N instead.

**take-stock intermediate TSV** (`take-stock.sh <root> --cards`, tab-separated, no header, 7 fields):

| # | Field           | Meaning                                                             |
| - | ---             | ---                                                                 |
| 1 | `kind`          | `repo`, `session`, or `handoff`                                     |
| 2 | `ref`           | repo-relative path of the card or handoff, empty on the `repo` row  |
| 3 | `status`        | session status, or handoff derived state, empty on the `repo` row   |
| 4 | `token`         | doc-grammar token (`I52`), or empty                                 |
| 5 | `title`         | one-line title, tabs and newlines collapsed to spaces               |
| 6 | `last_activity` | `YYYY-MM-DD` of the newest recorded activity for that row           |
| 7 | `marker`        | `went-stale` (repo row), `died-mid-work` (session row), or empty    |

Exactly one `repo` row is emitted, always first.
One `session` row per file in `docs/sessions/`, one `handoff` row per handoff whose derived state is `live`.

**Card TSV field 13** (extends the shipped 12-field contract in
`docs/plans/2026-09-02.I52.obsidian-board-mvp-plan.md`):

| #  | Field    | Meaning                                            |
| -- | ---      | ---                                                |
| 13 | `marker` | empty, `went-stale`, or `died-mid-work`            |

**Card sources and ids** (`board-cards.sh`, after Task 5):

| Source    | card_id                        | Column                                    |
| ---       | ---                            | ---                                       |
| tracker   | `<repo_key>#<token>`           | from the `agent:` label, as shipped       |
| git       | `<repo_key>#git`               | `next-up`                                 |
| session   | `<repo_key>#s-<file stem>`     | from `status`, per the mapping above      |
| handoff   | `<repo_key>#h-<file stem>`     | `handed-off`                              |
| closed    | `<repo_key>#<token>`           | `done`                                    |

### Task 3: `scripts/take-stock.sh` - derive recorded state

Depends on: Task 1, Task 2.

**Files (exclusive ownership):**
- Create: `scripts/take-stock.sh`
- Test: `tests/sessions/take-stock.sh`

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: `scripts/handoff-log.sh state <path>` from Task 2 (called script-relative, exactly as `lifecycle-lint.sh` does); the session card format from Task 1; git log and `docs/handoffs/` in the target repo.
- Produces:
  - `take-stock.sh <repo-root>` prints a human recorded-state report on stdout, exit 0. The report names, on its own labelled line each: the authoritative handoff (the newest live one, or `none`), the count of live handoffs, the open session card or `none open`, the newest closed session card with its status, the newest commit date and subject, the went-stale verdict with both dates, and a `next step:` line.
  - `take-stock.sh <repo-root> --cards` prints the 7-field intermediate TSV defined in Global constraints, exit 0.
  - Exit 2 on a usage error or an unreadable repo root.
- Constant: `DIED_MID_WORK_HOURS=24` declared at the top of the file with a one-line comment naming it a hardcoded visible threshold.

Behavior notes, each edge named:
- Recorded-state timestamp = the newest of: every session card's last activity, and each live handoff's filename date at `00:00:00Z`. With no session cards and no handoffs, recorded state is empty and the went-stale verdict is `no` (nothing to be stale against).
- The authoritative handoff is the newest live one by filename date; among same-date live handoffs the lexically last full filename wins, so the choice is deterministic when two handoffs share a day (as the seam-1 driving handoff and Task 7's next-thread handoff may).
- Clock conventions, pinned: session-card timestamps are ISO-8601 UTC by the card format; handoff filename dates are taken as calendar dates with no zone (they were written in the author's local day); the newest commit's date is read in UTC explicitly - `TZ=UTC git log -1 --date=format-local:'%Y-%m-%d' --pretty=%cd` (`format-local` renders in the exported zone; plain `format` would render in each commit's own zone) - so the went-stale day comparison never mixes a local commit day against a UTC recorded day.
- A session card's last activity = its `closed:` value when non-empty, else the timestamp of the newest `## Log` line, else its `session:` value. Every key is read with the repo's existing `fm()` shape (`grep -E "^<key>:" | head -1 | sed -E 's/^<key>:[[:space:]]*//; s/[[:space:]]*$//'`), so a key written as `closed: ` with a trailing space reads as empty.
- `went-stale` when the newest commit's `YYYY-MM-DD` is strictly later than the recorded-state date; day granularity, so a commit made minutes after recording is not stale.
- `died-mid-work` when a card's `status:` is `open` and its last activity is more than `DIED_MID_WORK_HOURS` hours before now.
- `next step:` = the `next:` value of the newest session card when non-empty, else the first action line of the authoritative handoff, else `none recorded`.
- A repo with no `docs/sessions/` or no `docs/handoffs/` directory produces the report with `none` in those lines and exits 0; the script never creates directories.
- A repo with no commits reports `newest commit: none` and a went-stale verdict of `no`.
- Every free-text field emitted into the TSV passes through `tr '\t\n' '  '`.
- Hour arithmetic uses epoch seconds from BSD `date -u -j -f '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ' <ts> +%s` with a GNU `date -u -d <ts> +%s` fallback, matching the BSD-first pattern in `board-cards.sh`'s `fmt_epoch`.

**Acceptance check:** `bash tests/sessions/take-stock.sh` exits 0 `[executed-check]`.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# take-stock.sh rebuilds recorded state from git, session cards, and handoffs: the human report
# names the authoritative handoff and the next step, --cards emits the 7-field intermediate TSV,
# an open card older than the 24-hour threshold marks died-mid-work, a closed card marks nothing,
# and a commit on a later calendar day than the recorded state marks went-stale.
set -uo pipefail
HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
REPO="$(cd "$HERE/../.." && pwd)"
TS="$REPO/scripts/take-stock.sh"
fail() { echo "FAIL: $1" >&2; exit 1; }
tmp="$(mktemp -d)"; trap 'rm -rf "$tmp"' EXIT
R="$tmp/repo"; mkdir -p "$R/docs/sessions" "$R/docs/handoffs"
git -C "$R" init -q; git -C "$R" config user.email a@b.c; git -C "$R" config user.name t

today="$(date -u '+%Y-%m-%d')"
now="$(date -u '+%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ')"
old="$(date -u -v-30H '+%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ' 2>/dev/null || date -u -d '30 hours ago' '+%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ')"
tomorrow="$(date -u -v+1d '+%Y-%m-%d' 2>/dev/null || date -u -d 'tomorrow' '+%Y-%m-%d')"

mkcard() {   # $1 filename  $2 status  $3 session-ts  $4 closed-ts (may be empty)  $5 last-log-ts
  cat > "$R/docs/sessions/$1" <<EOF
---
session_card: true
session: $3
token: I52
title: card $1
status: $2
closed: $4
why:
next: run the next task
---

# card $1

## Log

- $5 opened
EOF
}
mkcard "2026-09-05.I52.stalled.md" open "$old" "" "$old"

printf '# Handoff: older (#52)\n\n## Next actions\n\n- Do the older thing.\n' \

printf '# Handoff: authoritative (#52)\n\n## Next actions\n\n- Do the newest thing.\n' \

( cd "$R" && git add -A && git commit -qm "seed" )

rep="$(bash "$TS" "$R")" || fail "take-stock exited non-zero"
grep -q "$today.I52.authoritative.md" <<<"$rep" || fail "the report does not name the authoritative handoff"
grep -qi '^next step:' <<<"$rep" || fail "the report has no 'next step:' line"
grep -q 'run the next task' <<<"$rep" || fail "the next step was not taken from the session card"

rows="$(bash "$TS" "$R" --cards)" || fail "--cards exited non-zero"
awk -F'\t' 'NF!=7{exit 3}' <<<"$rows" || fail "a --cards row does not have 7 fields"
[ "$(awk -F'\t' '$1=="repo"' <<<"$rows" | grep -c .)" -eq 1 ] || fail "--cards must emit exactly one repo row"
[ "$(head -1 <<<"$rows" | cut -f1)" = repo ] || fail "the repo row must be emitted first"
[ "$(awk -F'\t' '$1=="handoff"' <<<"$rows" | grep -c .)" -eq 2 ] || fail "both live handoffs should emit a row"
[ "$(awk -F'\t' '$1=="handoff"{print $3}' <<<"$rows" | sort -u)" = live ] || fail "handoff rows are not derived live"
[ "$(awk -F'\t' '$1=="session"{print $7}' <<<"$rows")" = died-mid-work ] \
  || fail "an open card older than 24 hours did not mark died-mid-work"
[ "$(awk -F'\t' '$1=="repo"{print $7}' <<<"$rows")" = "" ] \
  || fail "recorded state is current for today, went-stale must be empty"

# a commit on a later calendar day than the recorded state makes the repo went-stale
echo x > "$R/f"
( cd "$R" && git add f && GIT_AUTHOR_DATE="${tomorrow}T12:00:00Z" GIT_COMMITTER_DATE="${tomorrow}T12:00:00Z" \
    git commit -qm "later work" )

grep -qi 'none' "$tmp/empty.out" || fail "an empty repo's report does not say none anywhere"

TS="$REPO/scripts/take-stock.sh"
fail() { echo "FAIL: $1" >&2; exit 1; }
tmp="$(mktemp -d)"; trap 'rm -rf "$tmp"' EXIT
R="$tmp/repo"; mkdir -p "$R/docs/sessions" "$R/docs/handoffs"
git -C "$R" init -q; git -C "$R" config user.email a@b.c; git -C "$R" config user.name t

today="$(date -u '+%Y-%m-%d')"
now="$(date -u '+%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ')"
old="$(date -u -v-30H '+%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ' 2>/dev/null || date -u -d '30 hours ago' '+%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ')"
tomorrow="$(date -u -v+1d '+%Y-%m-%d' 2>/dev/null || date -u -d 'tomorrow' '+%Y-%m-%d')"

mkcard() {   # $1 filename  $2 status  $3 session-ts  $4 closed-ts (may be empty)  $5 last-log-ts
  cat > "$R/docs/sessions/$1" <<EOF
---
session_card: true
session: $3
token: I52
title: card $1
status: $2
closed: $4
why:
next: run the next task
---

# card $1

## Log

- $5 opened
EOF
}
mkcard "2026-09-05.I52.stalled.md" open "$old" "" "$old"

printf '# Handoff: older (#52)\n\n## Next actions\n\n- Do the older thing.\n' \
  > "$R/docs/handoffs/2026-09-01.I52.older.md"
printf '# Handoff: authoritative (#52)\n\n## Next actions\n\n- Do the newest thing.\n' \
  > "$R/docs/handoffs/$today.I52.authoritative.md"
( cd "$R" && git add -A && git commit -qm "seed" )

rep="$(bash "$TS" "$R")" || fail "take-stock exited non-zero"
grep -q "$today.I52.authoritative.md" <<<"$rep" || fail "the report does not name the authoritative handoff"
grep -qi '^next step:' <<<"$rep" || fail "the report has no 'next step:' line"
grep -q 'run the next task' <<<"$rep" || fail "the next step was not taken from the session card"

rows="$(bash "$TS" "$R" --cards)" || fail "--cards exited non-zero"
awk -F'\t' 'NF!=7{exit 3}' <<<"$rows" || fail "a --cards row does not have 7 fields"
[ "$(awk -F'\t' '$1=="repo"' <<<"$rows" | grep -c .)" -eq 1 ] || fail "--cards must emit exactly one repo row"
[ "$(head -1 <<<"$rows" | cut -f1)" = repo ] || fail "the repo row must be emitted first"
[ "$(awk -F'\t' '$1=="handoff"' <<<"$rows" | grep -c .)" -eq 2 ] || fail "both live handoffs should emit a row"
[ "$(awk -F'\t' '$1=="handoff"{print $3}' <<<"$rows" | sort -u)" = live ] || fail "handoff rows are not derived live"
[ "$(awk -F'\t' '$1=="session"{print $7}' <<<"$rows")" = died-mid-work ] \
  || fail "an open card older than 24 hours did not mark died-mid-work"
[ "$(awk -F'\t' '$1=="repo"{print $7}' <<<"$rows")" = "" ] \
  || fail "recorded state is current for today, went-stale must be empty"

# a commit on a later calendar day than the recorded state makes the repo went-stale
echo x > "$R/f"
( cd "$R" && git add f && GIT_AUTHOR_DATE="${tomorrow}T12:00:00Z" GIT_COMMITTER_DATE="${tomorrow}T12:00:00Z" \
    git commit -qm "later work" )
[ "$(bash "$TS" "$R" --cards | awk -F'\t' '$1=="repo"{print $7}')" = went-stale ] \
  || fail "a commit on a later day than the recorded state did not mark went-stale"

# a closed card carries its terminal status and no marker
mkcard "2026-09-08.I52.closed.md" done "$now" "$now" "$now"
st="$(bash "$TS" "$R" --cards | awk -F'\t' '$2 ~ /closed.md$/ {print $3 "|" $7}')"
[ "$st" = "done|" ] || fail "a closed card should carry status done and no marker, got '$st'"

# an empty repo reports rather than failing
E="$tmp/empty"; mkdir -p "$E"; git -C "$E" init -q
bash "$TS" "$E" > "$tmp/empty.out" || fail "take-stock failed on a repo with no records"
grep -qi 'none' "$tmp/empty.out" || fail "an empty repo's report does not say none anywhere"
echo "PASS: report names the authoritative handoff and next step, 7-field --cards rows, died-mid-work at 24h, went-stale by day"
CANONICAL_TEST_EOF

# run the acceptance test, printing everything
bash tests/sessions/take-stock.sh; rc=$?
[ "$rc" -eq 0 ] || { echo "CHECK FAIL: acceptance test tests/sessions/take-stock.sh exited $rc; its output above names the failed assertion"; exit 1; }

# scoped regression gate (this task's suites only)
bash tests/sessions/take-stock.sh
rc=$?
[ "$rc" -eq 0 ] || { echo "CHECK FAIL: the scoped regression gate exited $rc; a suite this task can affect regressed"; exit 1; }

# ownership audit
git add -A
extra="$(git diff --cached --name-only | grep -vE '^(scripts/take\-stock\.sh|tests/sessions/take\-stock\.sh)$' || true)"
[ -z "$extra" ] || { echo "CHECK FAIL: files outside the ownership list were changed:"; printf '%s\n' "$extra"; exit 1; }

# portability audit on changed shell files
bad="$(git diff --cached --name-only | grep -E '\.sh$' | xargs grep -nE 'declare -A|\$\{[A-Za-z_]+,,\}|grep -P' 2>/dev/null || true)"
[ -z "$bad" ] || { echo "CHECK FAIL: bash 3.2 portability violation (associative array, lowercase expansion, or grep -P):"; printf '%s\n' "$bad"; exit 1; }

# export the patch outside the worktree
git diff --cached > "$PATCH"
[ -s "$PATCH" ] || { echo "CHECK FAIL: exported patch $PATCH is empty; the worker produced no applicable work"; exit 1; }
echo "CHECK PASS: The canonical take-stock suite passes: the report names the authoritative handoff and a next step, --cards emits 7-field rows with exactly one repo row first, died-mid-work marks at 24 hours, went-stale marks by calendar day, and an empty repo reports rather than failing."
